title: Warmup orchestration sim - scratchbook
content:
Context / motivation:
- This is a personal scratchpad to explore a small simulator for warmup/prefetch orchestration inside the serving runtime. Idea is to model how different warmup strategies (prefix prefetch, kv-cache seeding, token-level speculative prefetch) affect tail latency, token-cost, and cache hit rates for short interactive sessions.
- Want something lightweight we can iterate on and that maps to the runtime knobs we expose via the route config. Not a full-scale queuing sim (not yet) — focus on event-driven session traces + cache state and policy decisions.

Goals of the sim (MVP):
1) Fast feedback loop for trying new warmup heuristics against synthetic workload traces.
2) Produce metrics we currently expose in Console (per-route warmup hit-rate, avg warmup latency, extra tokens preloaded).
3) Generate candidate default configs for Optimize recommendations.

High-level architecture of sim (notes):
- Input: trace files (newline JSON per request); each trace entry has session_id, timestamp, prompt_prefix_tokens, expected continuation_length, user_priority, model_variant_hint
- Runtime model: a small discrete event loop that processes requests in time order. Keeps per-session KV cache state plus a global GPU warmup queue (limited parallelism).
- Policy layer: several warmup policies pluggable (see policy sketches below).
- Output: time-series of latency samples, token-cost delta, cache hit/miss counters, and per-session cold-start counts.

ASCII diagram (very rough):

  +-------------+      +------------+       +------------+
  | Trace input | ---> | Sim engine | --->  | Metrics/CSV |
  +-------------+      +------------+       +------------+
                             |
                             v
                    +--------------------+
                    | Policy (pluggable) |
                    +--------------------+
                             |
                 +-----------+-----------+
                 |                       |
                 v                       v
         KV-cache model            Warmup queue model

Key state abstractions (informal):
- SessionState: last_n_prefixes: ring buffer of token hashes; kv_keys: set[string]; last_request_ts; last_model_variant
- KVCache: map[kv_key -> (last_used_ts, size_bytes, generation)] with a global capacity and LRU-ish eviction
- WarmupQueue: entries (session_id, kv_keys_to_load, priority, scheduled_at, expected_gpu_ms)

Policy sketches (pluggable):
- policy A: On-request prefetch of exact KV keys for the prefix only. Conservative: only seed keys referenced by top-k attention window.
- policy B: Aggressive prefix expansion: prefetch prefix+N tokens (speculative) when session idle < idle_threshold. Trades token-cost for hit-rate.
- policy C: Model-variant-aware fallback: if preferred variant cold, prefetch a lightweight quantized variant first (fast, low-cost), then backfill full weights when GPU free.
- policy D: Budgeted warmup: global token budget per minute; prioritize by tenant priority and recency.

Example API shape for policy plugin (pseudo-Python):
- decide_warmup(session_state, incoming_request) -> WarmupPlan
  where WarmupPlan = {
    "kv_keys": ["k1","k2"],
    "estimated_tokens": "12",
    "priority": "high|normal|low",
    "expected_gpu_ms": "30"
  }
Notes: keep plan small and serializable. We want to store recent plans to replay traces.

Sample trace line (JSON) to feed sim:
{"session_id":"s-384","ts":1700001200.123,"prefix_tokens":[123,45,78],"continuation_len":64,"priority":"normal","model_hint":"glm-7b-v1"}

Mini-config DSL (route-level) to try in sim (YAML-ish):
route: chat.fast
warmup:
  enabled: true
  policy: budgeted
  budget_per_minute: 2000 # tokens
  idle_window_s: 2
  speculative_tokens: 8
  variant_fallback: ["quantized-8bit","fp16"]

Metrics to emit from one sim run:
- total_requests
- avg_latency_ms (user-visible)
- p95_latency_ms
- mean_warmup_overhead_ms (warmup scheduling costs that add to request latency)
- tokens_prefetched_total
- kv_cache_hit_rate (by first-request vs subsequent)
- extra_token_cost_per_1k_requests

Questions / open issues (todo):
- How accurate does the token-cost model need to be? For first pass, assume linear tokens*cost_per_token for warmup; later add model-variant weight load cost per GB.
- Where should the sim live? small Python package under tools/sim/warmup or an internal Rust micro-sim? Python fastest for experiments; could later port hot paths.
- Should we simulate GPU concurrency (context loads interfering)? MVP will model warmup queue with N parallel slots and simple backpressure.
- Do we need to model network egress (if KV loads fetch from remote store)? Might include an optional latency multiplier for remote KV.

Quick experiment plan (next steps I will run locally):
1) Implement trace loader + minimal event loop (Python).
2) Implement KVCache (LRU) + WarmupQueue.
3) Add two policies: conservative (A) and budgeted (D).
4) Generate synthetic traces: mix of short 1-3 turn sessions and long 20+ turn sessions, with varying idle gaps.
5) Run sweeps varying speculative_tokens and budget_per_minute.
6) Export CSV and quick Matplotlib plots (hit-rate vs p95).

Notes-to-self on heuristics:
- Small sessions (<=3 turns) are very sensitive to cold start; targeted prefix prefetch tends to help a lot at low cost.
- Long sessions benefit more from background fill (late prefetch) than immediate prefetch. Might bias policy by session_age.
- Tenant priority should be a first-class signal; default budgets otherwise get eaten by noisy users.

Example quick command to run sim (prototype):
python sim/run.py --trace traces/small_mix.jsonl --config experiments/budgeted-fast.yaml --out results/budgeted-fast.csv

Embeddable diagrams for internal notes (ASCII timeline):
TS ------>
[request A arrives] -- schedule warmup (k1,k2) --> warmup queue slot 1 occupied for 40ms --> request A continues with partial KV hit -> increased latency 12ms
[request B arrives] -------------------------> all warmup slots busy -> B suffers cold miss -> schedule optional fallback

Things to capture in PRD if this becomes a product feature:
- Config contract (YAML schema) for route warmup + audit trail of warmup plans.
- Observability: per-plan trace id and cost attribution for Optimize recommendations.
- Safeguards: global budget enforcement + tenant-level caps.

Random small ideas to test later:
- Use small ML classifier to predict which prefixes will be hot next, trained on past traces (very rough).
- Learn budget allocation per-tenant via multi-armed bandit with reward = reduction in p95 latency / token-cost.

References and quick links (to add to linked_artifacts later):

- Related sim: tools/trace-sim/ingress-sim (internal)
